problem_type: Conversation follow intent and viewport lifecycle ownership
symptom: Switching Agent conversations lands above the latest message; streaming and sending while reading earlier messages can leave the latest output out of view.
direct_cause: The previous panel retained a follow boolean across conversations and followed row-count dependencies instead of content height. Sending did not explicitly resume following.
class_root: No shared scroll owner distinguished explicit latest-message intent from reading intent and hidden-host restoration.
affected_population: Creation, canvas and timeline resident conversations
Streaming text, expanding cards, asynchronous history and panel collapse/expand
entry_points: Composer submit and jump-to-latest explicitly resume following
Scroll viewport handles older-history anchors and hidden-host restoration

external_sources.purpose: Installed 1.1.6 source owns content-height follow, user-scroll cancellation and explicit resume.

invariants: One useStickToBottom instance owns follow intent for every resident surface.
Conversation changes and sends explicitly request latest output; upward reading cancels follow.
History anchors write only while not following; collapse/expand preserves the prior reading position.

door_reduction.why_not: WorkbenchShell and the lab host must mount the resident host; the three design-lab fixtures and resident shell must render the shared panel. All call the same panel scroll boundary rather than implementing their own follow policy.

generality_proof: Every production surface renders ProjectAgentResidentShell and then AgentPanelV4Panel. The library follows actual content-height changes regardless of row kind or provider, while explicit conversation identity and submit/jump actions restore latest intent.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Bind the library scroll/content refs and all explicit follow and restoration events.
Supply project/surface/thread identity to the single panel.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: One AgentPanelV4Panel render supplies conversationKey composed from project, surface and session.
Fixtures render AgentPanelV4Panel directly and inherit the same scroll owner.

recurrence.reason: Any thread switch, new stream or hidden panel can repeat the stale-follow mechanism across all resident surfaces.
same_class_scan: door-map AgentPanelV4Panel: four reader files, one production shell.
door-map ProjectAgentResidentShell: WorkbenchShell and design-lab host.
Search for atBottomRef, flowScrollMemoryFor and residentTranscriptScroll confirms the previous owners are removed.
door-map useStickToBottom: one write owner in AgentPanelV4Panel; the library is the sole generic follow owner.

prevention.invariant: Follow content geometry through one library owner; explicit latest intent resumes following.
prevention.failure_mode: Upward reading releases follow; no fallback to the deleted row-count policy.
prevention.strategy: Replace the homemade generic follow policy, remove duplicate memory/dead policy, and register a framework boundary rejecting hand-rolled follow-bottom.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove per-thread memory and unused duplicate follow policy with their tests; panel owns only domain pagination and collapse restoration.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Replace generic scroll tracking with the installed content-height library.
exit_criteria: Retain while conversation landing, upward reading and hidden-host restoration regressions pass; reassess on a failing lifecycle regression or unsupported React version.

migration: No persisted schema changes. Scroll memory was in-process only. Switching surfaces now lands at latest output as does switching threads.
residual_risks: Real-provider user journey is unverified: only loopback fixtures are authorized.
Dock/float moves with exactly unchanged geometry may not trigger restoration.
Main/fixed walkthrough and performance measurements are pending execution.
